// Must-NOT-trip fixture: the two legal ".." shapes in this repo, recognised by
// SHAPE rather than by an exemption list — an exemption list would go stale the
// moment a fifth rev-range call site is added.
package scanfixture

import (
	"fmt"
	"strings"
)

// A git rev-list RANGE is string concatenation, not a path comparison. Four
// live sites have this shape: topology.go, basebranch.go, doctor.go and
// milestone.go.
func aheadCount(main, work string) []string {
	return []string{"rev-list", "--count", main + ".." + work}
}

func aheadOfOrigin(base string) []string {
	return []string{"rev-list", "origin/" + base + ".." + base}
}

// refguard's shape: strings.Contains over a REF name, in a function that makes
// no path call at all. git forbids ".." in a ref for its own reasons, which is
// a different rule from containment and must stay.
func validateGitRef(name string) error {
	if strings.Contains(name, "..") {
		return fmt.Errorf("unsafe git ref: %q contains \"..\"", name)
	}
	if strings.Contains(name, "@{") {
		return fmt.Errorf("unsafe git ref: %q contains \"@{\"", name)
	}
	return nil
}
